//: cleanUrls + trailingSlash keep exactly ONE spelling of each URL live: /docs, never /docs/ or /docs/index.html. Any second spelling that answers 200 is a duplicate of a page we are trying to get indexed. Vercel checks the filesystem before applying `rewrites`, so the prerendered dist/docs/index.html wins over the SPA catch-all below.

headers.//: The API keeps every security header the catch-all applies, and ONLY loses the Cache-Control override. Listed separately rather than left to the catch-all so that the omission of Cache-Control here is visibly deliberate: each handler sets its own, because only it knows whether the body is immutable (a revealed creature's traits) or transient (a chain read that failed).

`(?!api/)` matters and was missing. This rule matched /api/* too — no file extension, not under assets/ — and stamped `no-cache, must-revalidate` on every API response, overriding the Cache-Control each handler sets for itself. So the NFT metadata routes were uncacheable no matter what they asked for: no CDN in front could hold them, and every marketplace and wallet fetch reached the function. That is the shape of 2.1M edge requests against a site with no real visitors. The API keeps its security headers below; only the cache decision goes back to the handler, which is the only thing that knows whether a body is immutable (a revealed creature) or transient (an unresolved read).
